interface.note: engine frame: x forward, y left, z up, origin = crank axis; +y = output side (bike's left), -y = alternator side (bike's right)

steps.1: Upper case on a stand. Press the upper main shells and balance-shaft shells into their saddles.
steps.2: On the bench: fit the rod shells and bush, bolt the rod cap onto the crank pin with the two 7/16 rod bolts.
steps.3: Lower the crank and rod from below into the upper case, then the balance shaft (weights down).
steps.4: Fit the lower shells, set the bedplate on the upper case (add two dowel pins here in the real build, not modelled yet), fit and torque the M10 main-cap bolts and M8 case bolts.
steps.5: Set the piston on the rod small end from above, push the pin in from the side, fit the rings.
steps.6: Press the liner into the barrel, lower the barrel over the piston (ring compressor), then the head gasket.
steps.7: Head with valves, springs, retainers and keepers built on the bench; lower it onto the four studs, washers and nuts.
steps.8: Set the four followers on the valve tips, slide in the pivot shafts, lower the cams, fit the ladder and its bolts.
steps.9: Cam cover, spark plug and coil.
steps.10: Output side (+y, the bike's left): balance gear onto the shaft, water impeller, gear cover and pump cover, then the output flange.
steps.11: Alternator side (-y, the bike's right): oil pump rotors, crank sprocket, cam sprockets, chain with master link, guide, tensioner, trigger wheel, rotor, chain and alternator cover with stator.
steps.12: Oil pan, oil filter and throttle body.
